OK so they now have: Ornery Dilophosaur (2/2 deathtouch, sick), Scion Summoner (2/2, sick), 2x Eldrazi Scion (1/1, one sick). Everything has summoning sickness except one Scion. They're all tapped out.

Next turn I attack with everything. They'll have 4 blockers for my 4 attackers. Key play: attack all, they can only block 4. If they block Herald with the deathtouch dino, I lose Herald but everything else gets through. I can use Titanic Growth on an unblocked creature to push lethal.

Let me pass to my turn.

Just a 1/1 Scion attacking. I could block with my Elf Warrior Token 1/1 to trade, but I'd lose a body for next turn's alpha strike. Actually, they're at 6 and I have 9 power across 4 creatures. Even losing the token (1 power), I'd have 8 power across 3 attackers and Titanic Growth for +4. More than enough.

Let me trade the token to save 1 life — but actually, keeping more bodies is better because they have 4 blockers. If I have 4 attackers vs 4 blockers, they can block everything. If I only have 3 attackers, they still can block all 3. Hmm, the math:

With 4 attackers (2+3+1+3 = 9), they block all 4 with their 4 creatures. I can Titanic Growth an attacker after blocks. If I pump whoever is blocked by a 1/1 Scion, the overflow goes through as... wait, none of my creatures have trample except I can't.

Actually I need to think differently. They block all 4 of my creatures. Without trample, blocked creatures deal damage to blockers not to face. So I need unblocked creatures. If I have 4 attackers and they have 4 blockers, everything gets blocked and 0 damage gets through (without trample).

So keeping the token doesn't help if they block everything. Better to just not block here, take 1, and then next turn I need to figure out how to get damage through.

Wait — Herald has the Primeval Herald trigger. Let me re-check.

But the "sick" creatures — Ornery Dilophosaur and Scion Summoner — those entered on their turn 6 (their main phase). They'd have summoning sickness but that only affects attacking, not blocking. However, they're tapped from... wait, why would they be tapped?

I think the display might be from a different point. Let me just go to combat and see what happens. First, let me cast Ivy Lane Denizen before combat — it's a 2/3 that won't be able to attack (summoning sickness) but it's good to have on board for later.

- **Primeval Herald** (3/1) — UNBLOCKED! 3 damage gets through

So only 3 damage gets through. They go to 3. I lose Elite, Mentor, and Token. They lose all 3 blockers. 

But wait — I have Titanic Growth! Should I use it? Let me think...

If I pump Herald (+4/+4 = 7/5 trample), it's unblocked so it deals 7. That's overkill but wastes the Growth. 

What about pumping Elderleaf Mentor? It's blocked by the 2/2 deathtouch Dilophosaur. Even if I pump it to 7/6, deathtouch still kills it. No trample either, so no extra damage goes through. Bad.

What about pumping Dwynen's Elite? Blocked by 2/2 Scion Summoner. Pump to 6/6, kills the 2/2, but no trample — 0 extra damage. But Elite survives! That's decent.

Actually, the best play: pump Primeval Herald with Titanic Growth. It's unblocked. 7 damage to face instead of 3. They go to -1. That's lethal!

Wait, 3 unblocked + Titanic Growth (+4) = 7 total from Herald alone. They're at 6. 7 > 6. LETHAL!

annotations.description: Using Titan's Presence (premium colorless removal that can exile large threats) plus sacrificing the Eldrazi Scion token to remove a 2/2 Dwynen's Elite. While the opponent's only creature, it's not a major threat. Titan's Presence could be saved for a much larger threat later, and once Grk41F Timmy develops creatures (Ornery Dilophosaur, Scion Summoner), Savage Stomp could handle small-to-medium threats more efficiently.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Titan's Presence (sacrificing Scion token for mana) to exile Dwynen's Elite 2/2.
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn, play Warped Landscape or develop next turn with Cultivate/Scion Summoner, then use Savage Stomp to handle threats once you have creatures on board. Save Titan's Presence for larger threats that Savage Stomp can't handle.

annotations.description: Used Titan's Presence (an instant-speed removal spell) during main phase to remove a 2/2, when stuck on only 3 lands with Endbringer (6 mana) and other expensive spells in hand. Cultivate would ramp to 5 mana next turn and accelerate toward the game-winning Endbringer. The opponent's 2/2s are not urgent threats, and Titan's Presence could have been held for a bigger target later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Titan's Presence to exile a 2/2, spending all mana on removal while stuck on 3 lands.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Cultivate to ramp to 5 mana next turn (4 lands + Scion token), getting within striking distance of casting Endbringer. Hold Titan's Presence as instant-speed removal for a more threatening target.

annotations.description: Passed on casting Savage Stomp when the game engine indicated it was a legal play. With Ornery Dilophosaur (Dinosaur) as the target, the cost would be reduced to {G}. A 3/3 deathtouch Dilophosaur could fight and kill Primeval Herald 3/1 (trading) or fight and kill Dwynen's Elite 2/2 (surviving as a 3/1). Either way, removing a threat - especially the dangerous Primeval Herald that ramps lands every attack - would be highly valuable.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting Savage Stomp, leaving the opponent's threats intact.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Savage Stomp targeting Ornery Dilophosaur and Primeval Herald 3/1 (or Dwynen's Elite 2/2). Killing Primeval Herald prevents future land ramp and removes a 3-power attacker. Even trading the Dilophosaur for Herald is a good deal given the Herald's value.

annotations.description: Casting Savage Stomp during combat targeting the Eldrazi Scion Token (the only creature controlled) is problematic. The Scion likely needs to be sacrificed for mana to pay for the spell (only 1-2 untapped lands vs 3 mana cost), which would cause the spell to fizzle. Even if it resolves, a 2/2 Scion fighting into Primeval Herald 3/1 results in losing the Scion while Herald survives, or trading with Dwynen's Elite - poor value for a removal spell. Savage Stomp should be saved for when bigger creatures like Ornery Dilophosaur (discount as Dinosaur, reducing cost to {G}) or Colossal Dreadmaw are on board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Savage Stomp during combat with only a 1/1 Eldrazi Scion Token on board
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority, let the Scion deal 1 combat damage, then in postcombat main phase develop the board with Scion Summoner (if mana allows) and save Savage Stomp for when Ornery Dilophosaur is in play (costs only {G} targeting a Dinosaur) for much better value.

annotations.description: Cast Might of the Masses in response to opponent's Colossal Dreadmaw being cast, with no combat happening and both of their creatures tapped. The pump spell (+1/+1 per creature) will expire at end of turn having accomplished nothing, wasting a card that could have been a significant combat trick later.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Might of the Masses in response to Colossal Dreadmaw on the stack, pumping a tapped creature with no combat.
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority and let the Dreadmaw resolve. Save Might of the Masses for a future combat step where it could help trade favorably or push through damage. Combined with Band Together or Titanic Growth, these combat tricks represent significant reach that shouldn't be wasted.

annotations.description: Band Together with Dwynen's Elite (2 power) + Primeval Herald (3 power) deals only 5 damage total to the 6/6 Colossal Dreadmaw, leaving it alive at 1 toughness. This wastes the Band Together spell without killing the main threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Band Together targeting own creatures (2+3=5 power) against Colossal Dreadmaw (6 toughness), which doesn't kill it.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Titanic Growth on Primeval Herald first (making it 7/5), then cast Band Together with just the pumped Primeval Herald targeting Dreadmaw for 7 damage, cleanly killing it. Alternatively, Titanic Growth on Dwynen's Elite (6/6) and Band Together with both creatures for 9 total damage.

annotations.description: Band Together was cast in response to Might of the Masses (on the stack), meaning it resolves BEFORE Might of the Masses. Primeval Herald is still 3/1, so Band Together deals only 2+3=5 damage to Colossal Dreadmaw (6 toughness), failing to kill it. If they had let Might of the Masses resolve first (giving Herald +2/+2 to 5/3), then cast Band Together, it would deal 2+5=7 damage, killing the Dreadmaw. The Dreadmaw is a massive threat that will dominate the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Band Together in response to Might of the Masses, before the pump resolved
annotations.betterLine: Pass priority to let Might of the Masses resolve (making Primeval Herald 5/3), then cast Band Together targeting Dwynen's Elite and Primeval Herald to deal 7 total damage to Colossal Dreadmaw, killing it

annotations.description: Opponent is at 11 life with all lands tapped and no blockers. Casting Titanic Growth on an unblocked attacker would deal 9 total instead of 5, putting opponent to 2 life instead of 6. At 2 life, virtually any creature getting through next turn is lethal, making it nearly impossible for the opponent to stabilize. At 6 life, the opponent has much more room to deploy blockers and survive. The Growth is guaranteed to connect here with zero risk of being blown out.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to cast Titanic Growth on an unblocked attacker
annotations.betterLine: Cast Titanic Growth on Primeval Herald (making it 7/5 trample) or Dwynen's Elite (making it 6/6) to deal 9 damage total, putting opponent to 2 life where almost any follow-up is lethal

annotations.description: Opponent is at 6 life with all lands tapped and no untapped blockers. Attacking with Dwynen's Elite (2/2) and Primeval Herald (3/1) deals only 5 damage, leaving opponent at 1. Casting Titanic Growth (+4/+4) on either attacker would deal 9 total damage — lethal. Opus Brewer had 3 untapped Forests, more than enough mana for Titanic Growth (1G).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without casting Titanic Growth, dealing only 5 of the needed 6 damage.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Titanic Growth on either attacking creature for guaranteed lethal damage (9 total vs 6 life).

annotations.description: At 6 life facing 9 power of attackers (lethal next turn), Timmy cast Ornery Dilophosaur (2/2 deathtouch) instead of Endbringer (5/5 with untap-during-opponent's-turn ability). Endbringer would be a much better stabilizer - it blocks and survives combat with any of the opponent's creatures, and can tap down an attacker during opponent's turn since it untaps on their untap step. The Dilophosaur can only trade with one creature, leaving Timmy still facing lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Endbringer (5/5 for {5}{C}, using Eldrazi Scion for colorless). Endbringer blocks profitably, untaps on opponent's turn to tap down an additional attacker, and provides card draw/ping utility to stabilize the dire board state.

annotations.description: At 6 life facing potential lethal next turn (9+ damage from opponent's creatures), Timmy chose Scion Summoner over Savage Stomp. Savage Stomp costs only {G} targeting the Ornery Dilophosaur (Dinosaur discount), putting a +1/+1 counter on it and using deathtouch to kill any opposing creature (like Elderleaf Mentor 3/2). This both removes an attacker AND creates a 3/3 deathtouch blocker, far more impactful for survival. With Savage Stomp costing only {G}, Timmy would still have {G}{G} remaining — not enough for Scion Summoner but still a much better defensive position.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Scion Summoner to add a 2/2 body and 1/1 Scion token as blockers.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Savage Stomp for {G} targeting Ornery Dilophosaur and an opponent's creature (likely Elderleaf Mentor 3/2), killing it with deathtouch while buffing Dilophosaur to 3/3. This removes a major threat and creates a powerful deathtouch blocker for surviving the next attack.

annotations.description: At 6 life, Grk41F Timmy used the deathtouch Ornery Dilophosaur to block Elderleaf Mentor (3/2) instead of Primeval Herald (3/1). Primeval Herald is far more dangerous as it fetches a land every attack and has been generating incremental advantage. The chosen blocks let Herald survive and dealt 3 damage (to 3 life), while the better line would kill Herald, take only 2 damage (to 4 life), and leave the less threatening Elderleaf Mentor alive.
annotations.actionTaken: Ornery Dilophosaur (deathtouch) blocked Elderleaf Mentor, Scion Summoner blocked Dwynen's Elite, Eldrazi Scion blocked Elf Warrior Token — Primeval Herald gets through for 3.
annotations.betterLine: Ornery Dilophosaur (deathtouch) should block Primeval Herald (3/1) to kill it, Scion Summoner blocks Elderleaf Mentor (dies but absorbs 3 damage), Eldrazi Scion blocks Elf Warrior Token — only Dwynen's Elite (2/2) gets through for 2 damage, going to 4 life instead of 3, and the most threatening creature is removed.

annotations.description: Cast Titanic Growth during combat when already attacking for 9 damage against an opponent at 6 life with no available blockers (all potential blockers are either sick or tapped) and all opponent lands tapped. The spell accomplishes nothing since lethal damage is already guaranteed.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Titanic Growth on an attacker for +4/+4 when already dealing lethal damage
annotations.betterLine: Don't cast Titanic Growth — save it (though irrelevant since the game is won). The 9 unblocked damage is already lethal against 6 life.
